correctness.rationale: For real gamma<=1 and sigma>0, V=(x²+y²+(2−gamma)z²/sigma)/2 is positive definite and radially unbounded. Independent SymPy expansion of grad(V)·f +x²+(y−z)²+(1−gamma)z² gave exactly zero. For gamma<1 the dissipation is negative definite, implying global existence and GAS. At gamma=1 the zero-derivative set {x=0,y=z} has only the origin as invariant subset because xdot=y², so LaSalle proves all-solution convergence. For gamma>1, substitution of E±=(gamma−1,±sqrt(gamma−1),±sqrt(gamma−1)) into all three field components is exactly zero, prohibiting global attraction. Invariant compactly supported stationary measures are delta_origin, by integrating the nonnegative derivative defect and support invariance; equivalently global convergence and bounded convergence imply the same for any invariant probability. Normalization and endpoint are respected. No claim for controlled/load-forced PMSM, nor rates at gamma=1. The included verifier algebra is consistent but is not independent external certification.

originality.rationale: The full closed global-attraction claim is already implied by published Lorenz results. Zhang–Liao–Mu (2017), Remark 1(i), explicitly gives the exact coordinate swap (X,Y,Z)=(z,y,x) from this uncontrolled PMSM system to Lorenz with r=gamma,b=1. Kuznetsov–Mokaev–Kuznetsova–Kudryashova (2020), Theorem 1 and proof case r<=1, establishes all Lorenz trajectories converge to the unique origin for 0<r<=1 and every sigma>0,b=1; the endpoint follows by the standard invariant-set argument even though the article prints a strict derivative sign there. The regime r>1 has explicit nonzero equilibria, so no global attraction. The claimed compact invariant-probability rigidity follows as a general corollary of global attraction by invariance and bounded convergence for test functions, irrespective of whether this exact wording appears in prior papers. Negative gamma is outside the 2020 physical-positive-r statement but is a routine extension of the same classical quadratic argument, not a new motivated mathematical phenomenon. This is mathematical implication coverage, not a bibliographic title match.
residual_risks: Kuznetsov et al. (2020) state a strict negative derivative at r=1 that is only semidefinite in some nonzero directions. The critical claim remains provable by an independent LaSalle/Barbashin–Krasovskii invariant-set check; this is a proof-presentation caveat, not a priority gap.

Lorenz paper uses r>0 physically. gamma<=0 is outside that stated domain, but the submitted proof extends the established Lyapunov cancellation mechanically; no independent motivation was offered for a new result restricted to negative gamma.
A full bibliographic survey of older Lorenz literature is unnecessary to disprove originality since explicit published covering results were already read.

value.rationale: As a mathematical finding, the sharp origin global-attraction threshold is already a standard classical Lorenz result transported by the exact variable permutation explicitly published for this PMSM in 2017. The invariant probability assertion is an immediate generic consequence of convergence to a single equilibrium, not a new structural invariant or separately motivated classification. The gamma<=0 endpoint extension is the same elementary energy calculation and was not motivated as a distinct physical or mathematical gap. This is a useful engineering restatement but the claimed research contribution amounts to known theorem specialization/renaming plus a routine corollary, which does not meet the mathematical-value bar independently of correctness. This judgment is not based on the size of the result or on computational reproducibility.

limitations: Positive-parameter Lorenz coverage is decisive; negative gamma is outside prior physically positive-r assumptions, but routine Lyapunov extension under the same formula does not give a separately motivated contribution.
